university_name: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi)

overview.established_year: 1961 (originating as the College of Engineering & Technology, later declared an Institution of National Importance under the Institutes of Technology (Amendment) Act, 1963 and renamed IIT Delhi)
overview.location: Hauz Khas, New Delhi, Delhi, India
overview.type: Public/Government, Institute of National Importance and Deemed University
overview.campus_size: Approximately 320 acres urban campus in Hauz Khas, South Delhi
overview.description: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) is one of India’s premier Institutes of National Importance, established in 1961 as the College of Engineering & Technology and later brought under the Institutes of Technology Act to function as an autonomous, degree‑granting IIT with full academic and administrative powers.[1] Located in Hauz Khas, South Delhi, the institute occupies a sprawling, self‑contained 300+ acre campus that integrates academic buildings, laboratories, hostels, residential areas, sports facilities, and green spaces, creating an ecosystem that feels like a small technologically driven township within the capital city.[1][7] Historically, IIT Delhi emerged through Indo‑UK collaboration, with the British government and the Federation of British Industries supporting the creation of the Delhi Engineering College Trust and the development of the Hauz Khas campus, reflecting early international cooperation in shaping India’s higher technical education.[1][3] Over the decades, IIT Delhi has evolved from a primarily undergraduate engineering college to a broad‑based, research‑intensive technological university with strong programs in engineering, sciences, design, management, and interdisciplinary areas, consistently ranked among the top engineering institutions in India and well regarded internationally.[1][7] The institute is noted for its rigorous academic curriculum, competitive entry through national examinations such as JEE (Advanced) and GATE, and a culture that emphasizes both strong theoretical foundations and hands‑on problem solving, which has produced a large alumni network of influential technologists, entrepreneurs, academics, and policy leaders.[1][5] Its research profile spans cutting‑edge domains including artificial intelligence, communications and signal processing, renewable energy, nanotechnology, materials science, biotechnology, transportation systems, and public policy, with many faculty‑led centers of excellence and industry‑funded laboratories that contribute to national missions and global scientific literature.[1][7] Campus culture at IIT Delhi is known for being intellectually intense yet vibrant, with numerous technical societies, cultural clubs, entrepreneurship cells, and student‑run festivals such as Rendezvous and Tryst, which attract participants from institutions across India and offer a platform for innovation, arts, and leadership development.[1][8] The institute plays a key role in national development by providing high‑quality technical manpower, collaborating with government agencies and industry on strategic projects, incubating startups through its technology business incubators and research parks, and advising on policy issues related to infrastructure, digital transformation, energy, and sustainability.[1][5] In recent years, IIT Delhi has increased its global engagement through international joint degree programs, research partnerships, student and faculty exchanges, and membership in global academic networks, thereby strengthening its reputation as a globally connected yet nationally rooted institution.[7] Collectively, IIT Delhi’s historical legacy, academic excellence, strong placement outcomes, entrepreneurial ecosystem, and location in India’s political and administrative capital make it one of the most sought‑after destinations for science and engineering education in the country and a critical pillar in India’s knowledge and innovation landscape.[1][5][7]

rankings: NIRF 2024 Engineering: Consistently ranked among the top engineering institutions in India; in recent NIRF Engineering rankings, IIT Delhi has typically featured within the top 3–5 engineering institutes nationally, reflecting strong performance in teaching, learning resources, research output, graduation outcomes, and perception indicators.

NIRF 2024 Overall / University: In the overall and university‑specific categories, IIT Delhi has also been placed among the country’s leading institutions, indicating its comprehensive strength beyond engineering through contributions in sciences, management, design, and interdisciplinary research, as measured by NIRF criteria such as outreach and inclusivity, research funding, and professional practice.

QS World University Rankings (recent cycle): IIT Delhi has been regularly featured in the QS World University Rankings within the top global universities, often appearing among the top Indian institutions, highlighting its international academic reputation, employer reputation, faculty‑student ratio, and research citations per faculty, as well as growing global visibility of its programs.

QS World University Rankings by Subject – Engineering & Technology: In QS subject rankings, IIT Delhi is typically placed prominently in the global band for Engineering & Technology, reflecting strong citation impact, international collaborations, and employer recognition of its graduates in core engineering and technological disciplines.

QS World University Rankings by Subject – Computer Science & Information Systems: IIT Delhi’s computer science‑related programs have historically appeared in QS subject rankings for Computer Science and Information Systems, indicating a robust research environment in algorithms, systems, AI/ML, networks, and data science, as well as solid industry linkages and graduate outcomes.

Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings – Engineering & Technology: IIT Delhi has figured in THE rankings for Engineering & Technology, which evaluate teaching, research volume and influence, industry income, and international outlook, underscoring the institute’s role as a major global player in engineering higher education and research from India.

National and sectoral rankings for innovation and entrepreneurship: IIT Delhi is widely regarded as one of the top Indian campuses for innovation and entrepreneurship, frequently recognized in national innovation rankings, startup ecosystem assessments, and government or industry evaluations that consider patents filed, startups incubated, technology transfer, and industry collaboration activities.

Reputation among employers and academia: Across various national and international surveys, IIT Delhi consistently scores highly in employer reputation and academic reputation indicators, reflecting long‑standing confidence among recruiters, research partners, and peer institutions in the quality, skills, and adaptability of its graduates and the impact of its research programs.

Category‑wise recognition among Institutes of National Importance: Within the cohort of Institutes of National Importance and the IIT system, IIT Delhi is often grouped in the top tier alongside a few other longstanding IITs, based on historical prestige, breadth of programs, competitiveness of admissions, research funding, doctoral output, and influence of alumni in industry and academia.

Domain‑specific recognitions and awards: Individual departments and centers of IIT Delhi, such as those in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, civil engineering, computer science, physics, and management studies, have earned separate recognition through discipline‑specific surveys, professional society rankings, and government evaluations, affirming high standards in teaching, research, and professional practice at the department level.

B.Tech.course_name: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
B.Tech.duration: 4 Years (8 semesters, full‑time residential undergraduate program)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: For Indian nationals, tuition fees in recent years for B.Tech programs at IITs have generally been in the range of approximately INR 1–2 lakh per semester, with additional charges for hostel, mess, examination, and other institute facilities; the exact fee for IIT Delhi’s CSE program varies by academic year and category, with significant subsidies and fee waivers or scholarships available for students from economically weaker sections, reserved categories, and other eligible groups as per Government of India and institute norms.
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission to the B.Tech CSE program at IIT Delhi is primarily through the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Advanced, which is open to candidates who first qualify the national JEE Main examination conducted by the designated testing agency; aspirants must meet age limits, attempt limits, and minimum performance criteria in Class XII or equivalent examinations (with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics) as specified in the official JEE Advanced brochure, and final admission is based on All India Rank in JEE Advanced, seat allocation through JoSAA counseling, satisfaction of category‑wise cut‑off ranks (which for CSE at IIT Delhi are typically among the most competitive in the country), and fulfillment of documentation and medical fitness requirements.

B.Tech.duration: 4 Years (8 semesters, full‑time residential undergraduate program)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee structure for B.Tech in Electrical Engineering at IIT Delhi is aligned with the general B.Tech fee framework of the IIT system, with semester‑wise tuition in the approximate range of INR 1–2 lakh for general category Indian students, supplemented by hostel, mess, and other institutional fees; fee concessions, scholarships, and financial aid are available based on family income, category status (SC/ST/OBC‑NCL/EWS), and other government‑mandated policies, and foreign or sponsored students may have a different fee schedule as notified by the institute each year.
B.Tech.eligibility: Eligibility requires completion of Class XII or equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, along with meeting the JEE Main qualification criteria followed by appearance in JEE Advanced; admission is awarded through centralized JoSAA counseling strictly on the basis of JEE Advanced All India Rank, with IIT Delhi’s Electrical Engineering branch typically demanding very high ranks due to strong demand, and candidates must satisfy category‑wise cut‑offs, reservation policies, and institute‑specific requirements such as original certificates verification and medical fitness before registration.

B.Tech.duration: 4 Years (8 semesters, full‑time residential undergraduate program)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: Tuition charges for the B.Tech Mechanical Engineering program follow the standard B.Tech fee pattern at IIT Delhi, generally amounting to a cumulative tuition cost in the tens of lakhs of rupees over four years for general category students before accounting for subsidies, while actual payable amounts may be substantially reduced through income‑based fee waivers, scholarships, education loans, and support schemes operated by the Government of India and the institute; students additionally pay for accommodation, food, and miscellaneous institute services.
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is through JEE Advanced after qualifying JEE Main, with academic eligibility including a recognized senior secondary qualification featuring Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics and meeting minimum aggregate percentage or rank criteria as prescribed in the JEE information brochure; JoSAA’s centralized seat allocation process assigns seats based on JEE Advanced rank and preferences, and IIT Delhi’s Mechanical Engineering program typically has competitive cut‑offs, with candidates required to comply with reservation norms, category documentation, and medical fitness standards.

B.Tech.duration: 4 Years (8 semesters, full‑time residential undergraduate program)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee for B.Tech Civil Engineering at IIT Delhi is comparable to that of other B.Tech disciplines at the institute, with a per‑semester tuition component, hostel rent, mess charges, and institute fees that together constitute the total cost of education; many students benefit from merit‑cum‑means scholarships, fee waivers, or external sponsorships, and precise figures are announced annually by the institute and may differ for Indian nationals, foreign nationals, and sponsored candidates.
B.Tech.eligibility: Candidates must qualify JEE Main and then JEE Advanced, satisfy age and attempt limits, and have completed Class XII or equivalent with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, meeting any specified percentage criteria; admission is through JoSAA counseling based on JEE Advanced rank and category, with IIT Delhi’s Civil Engineering program attracting strong interest from students inclined towards infrastructure, structural engineering, and environmental engineering, and seats being filled in accordance with national reservation policy and institute regulations.

B.Tech.course_name: Integrated Dual Degree (B.Tech + M.Tech) programs (various engineering branches)
B.Tech.duration: 5 Years (10 semesters, integrated undergraduate + postgraduate program)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: For integrated dual degree programs, the fee structure is broadly similar to B.Tech fees on a per‑semester basis for the first four years, with tuition, hostel, and other charges announced annually, while the fifth year is treated as part of the integrated curriculum with corresponding tuition; over five years, the cumulative tuition is higher than a standalone B.Tech but typically lower than pursuing separate B.Tech and M.Tech degrees, and students may access scholarships, stipends in later years, or assistantships subject to institute policies.
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission criteria are aligned with B.Tech programs and are based primarily on performance in JEE Advanced following qualification in JEE Main, with candidates listing dual degree options during JoSAA counseling; cut‑offs for specific dual degree branches vary but are often comparable to or slightly lower than corresponding four‑year B.Tech branches, and students must meet the same board examination requirements, category‑wise reservation rules, and medical fitness standards as other undergraduate entrants at IIT Delhi.

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech (various specializations such as Computer Technology, Communication Systems, Mechanical Design, Structural Engineering, Power Electronics, etc.)
M.Tech.duration: 2 Years (4 semesters, full‑time postgraduate program; some part‑time options may also exist in select areas)
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: M.Tech tuition fees at IIT Delhi are typically lower per semester than undergraduate fees for Indian nationals, reflecting government support for postgraduate technical education, with additional charges for hostel, mess, and institute services; many M.Tech students receive financial assistance in the form of monthly stipends under Teaching/Research Assistantship schemes funded by government agencies, subject to fulfilling academic performance and workload requirements, thereby offsetting the effective cost of study.
M.Tech.eligibility: Admission to M.Tech programs usually requires a relevant bachelor’s degree in engineering or technology (or a related discipline) with a minimum specified percentage or CGPA, along with a valid GATE score in an appropriate paper; shortlisting and selection processes may involve cutoff GATE scores, written tests, and/or interviews conducted by departments, and sponsored candidates from industry or government organizations may be admitted under separate categories with different requirements, while reservation rules for SC/ST/OBC‑NCL/EWS/PwD categories are followed as per Government of India norms.

MBA.course_name: MBA (Master of Business Administration) – offered through Department of Management Studies (DMS), IIT Delhi
MBA.duration: 2 Years (4 semesters, full‑time residential management program)
MBA.total_tuition_fee: The MBA program at IIT Delhi, offered by the Department of Management Studies, follows a fee structure similar to that of leading public management institutions in India, with total program fees typically amounting to several lakhs of rupees including tuition and other academic charges, but remaining competitive relative to many private business schools; the fee is payable in installments each semester, and students may access educational loans, institute‑level merit scholarships, or corporate sponsorships depending on their profile and opportunities.
MBA.eligibility: Admission to the MBA program generally requires a bachelor’s degree in any discipline with a minimum percentage or CGPA as specified by DMS, along with a competitive score in a national‑level management aptitude test such as the Common Admission Test (CAT); shortlisted candidates are invited for further evaluation through group discussions, written ability tests, and personal interviews, and final selection considers multiple criteria including CAT score, academic record, work experience, diversity factors, and performance in the selection process, while reservation policies for different categories are implemented according to Government of India regulations.

Other Programs.course_name: M.Sc (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and other science disciplines as offered)
Other Programs.duration: 2 Years (4 semesters, full‑time postgraduate science program)
Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: Fees for M.Sc programs at IIT Delhi are generally modest relative to engineering programs, as they are heavily subsidized public higher education offerings in the pure sciences, with students paying tuition, hostel, and miscellaneous fees at levels comparable to or lower than many private institutions; some students may also receive scholarships or fellowships funded by external agencies (such as national science fellowships) depending on their academic performance and category.
Other Programs.eligibility: Admission to M.Sc programs is typically through national‑level examinations such as the Joint Admission Test for M.Sc (JAM) or other centralized tests recognized by IIT Delhi, with candidates required to hold a relevant bachelor’s degree (for example, B.Sc with appropriate subject combinations) and meet specified minimum marks or CGPA; final admission is based on all‑India rank in the entrance examination, fulfillment of category‑wise cut‑offs, document verification, and compliance with institute eligibility criteria for the specific discipline.

Other Programs.course_name: Ph.D. (Doctor of Philosophy) – Engineering, Sciences, Humanities & Social Sciences, Management, and Interdisciplinary areas
Other Programs.duration: Typically 3–5 Years (minimum and maximum durations vary by discipline and candidate status, with full‑time and part‑time options)
Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: Ph.D. candidates at IIT Delhi pay semester‑wise tuition and institute fees that are generally modest compared to professional coursework programs, as doctoral education is primarily research‑oriented and frequently supported through fellowships and assistantships funded by government bodies (such as MHRD/AICTE/UGC/CSIR/DBT), industry‑sponsored projects, or institute funds; full‑time Ph.D. scholars commonly receive monthly stipends and contingency grants, significantly reducing the net cost of pursuing advanced research at the institute.
Other Programs.eligibility: Eligibility for Ph.D. admission usually requires a master’s degree in a relevant field (M.Tech, M.E., M.Sc, M.A., MBA, or equivalent) with a minimum CGPA or percentage, or in some cases a bachelor’s degree with exceptional performance, along with evidence of research aptitude; many departments consider national‑level qualification examinations such as GATE, UGC‑NET, CSIR‑NET, or equivalent, and the admission process involves shortlisting based on academic record and test scores followed by written tests and/or interviews conducted by departmental selection committees, with separate provisions for sponsored, part‑time, and external candidates, and implementation of statutory reservation policies.

placements.description: The placement scenario at IIT Delhi is widely regarded as one of the strongest in India, with the institute attracting a large and diverse pool of recruiters across sectors such as software, information technology, core engineering, consulting, finance, analytics, product management, research and development, and fast‑growing startups, resulting in high placement rates for eligible students in both undergraduate and postgraduate programs. Over successive placement seasons, IIT Delhi has consistently reported strong average and median salary packages that reflect both the premium attached to IIT Delhi’s brand and the high demand for its graduates’ technical and analytical skills, with domestic compensation figures often ranking among the top in the country for engineering institutions. In addition to domestic offers, students at IIT Delhi regularly receive international job offers from technology firms, financial institutions, and multinational corporations, including roles in North America, Europe, and Asia‑Pacific, which significantly raise the highest package figures reported in annual statistics and illustrate the global employability of its graduates. The placement process is structured in phases, with pre‑placement talks, internships converting to pre‑placement offers (PPOs), and final interviews, and the institute’s dedicated Training and Placement Cell works closely with departments, student coordinators, and employers to schedule visits, shortlist candidates, and streamline interview logistics. Internship opportunities are an integral part of IIT Delhi’s placement ecosystem, with many students in their pre‑final year undertaking summer internships in leading companies and research labs, both in India and abroad; a significant proportion of these internships result in PPOs, which provide job security early and demonstrate employers’ confidence in the institute’s training. Placement trends over recent years show increasing interest from product‑based technology companies, high‑frequency trading firms, fintech startups, and global consulting majors, alongside stable recruitment from core engineering sectors such as construction, manufacturing, automotive, power, and telecommunications, giving students a wide choice of career paths aligned with their interests and specialization. For postgraduate students, including M.Tech, M.Sc, and MBA cohorts, the placement outcomes are also robust, with specialized roles in research and development, technical consulting, data science, product management, operations, and management consulting that leverage their advanced technical or managerial expertise. The institute’s alumni network plays a significant role in sustaining strong placement performance, as many alumni occupy senior positions in leading firms and frequently facilitate recruitment drives, internship collaborations, live projects, and industry‑academia partnerships that further enhance the placement ecosystem. Career support at IIT Delhi goes beyond the core placement season, with the institute and student bodies organizing resume‑building workshops, mock interviews, coding and case‑interview practice sessions, and sessions with alumni across sectors to help students prepare strategically for competitive selection processes. Overall, IIT Delhi’s placement record, characterized by high placement percentages, attractive salary packages, strong internship pipelines, and a broad mix of recruiting organizations, reinforces its reputation as a top destination for students seeking both high‑impact technical education and excellent career opportunities in India and abroad.
placements.highest_package: The highest packages offered in recent IIT Delhi placement seasons have typically been very high, especially for a small number of international and niche domestic roles in sectors such as global technology firms, quantitative finance, and high‑frequency trading; these headline figures, while representing only a fraction of total offers, underscore the institute’s ability to place top performers in highly competitive global roles.
placements.average_package: Average packages for core B.Tech branches and popular postgraduate programs at IIT Delhi have generally been among the highest in the country for engineering and technology institutions, reflecting sustained recruiter demand and the strong skill set of graduates; exact numeric values vary by branch, degree program, and year, but they are typically well above the national engineering graduate average, indicating a favorable return on investment for students.
major_recruiters: Various high‑frequency trading and quantitative finance firms (e.g., Tower Research, Jane Street, etc., depending on year)

facilities: Central Library: IIT Delhi maintains a large, modern central library that houses an extensive collection of printed books, reference works, technical reports, standards, bound journals, and theses across engineering, sciences, humanities, and management, complemented by access to a wide range of electronic databases, e‑journals, and e‑books; the library offers reading rooms, digital resource centers, study carrels, interlibrary loan services, and extended working hours during examination periods to support intensive academic and research activities.

Departmental Libraries and Resource Centers: In addition to the central library, many academic departments and centers maintain their own specialized libraries or resource rooms that focus on discipline‑specific literature, laboratory manuals, standards, and project reports, providing convenient access to highly relevant materials for students and researchers within the department and often serving as hubs for seminar series, reading groups, and research discussions.

Hostel Facilities: The residential campus includes multiple hostels for male and female students, each equipped with furnished rooms, common rooms with televisions and recreational facilities, internet connectivity, laundry areas, and dining halls (messes); hostel life forms a core aspect of IIT Delhi’s culture, with student‑run bodies managing many aspects of hostel governance, cultural events, inter‑hostel competitions, and peer support networks, fostering a close‑knit and collaborative community.

Dining and Mess Services: Each hostel is associated with its own mess providing daily meals, snacks, and beverages at subsidized rates, while the campus also hosts canteens, food courts, cafes, and street‑food style outlets that offer diverse cuisines and extended hours; the variety of food options supports students’ needs during late‑night study sessions and accommodates dietary preferences and constraints of a diverse student body.

Advanced Research Laboratories: IIT Delhi hosts numerous specialized research laboratories within departments such as Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Physics, and others, as well as interdisciplinary centers; these labs are equipped with advanced instrumentation, computing resources, experimental setups, prototyping tools, clean rooms, and test facilities that enable cutting‑edge research in fields like microelectronics, communications, robotics, materials science, and renewable energy.

Computer and IT Infrastructure: The campus has robust computing facilities, including departmental computer labs, high‑performance computing clusters, and institute‑wide IT services that provide high‑speed wired and wireless internet connectivity, email services, and access to licensed software tools; this infrastructure supports academic coursework, large‑scale simulations, data analysis, online learning platforms, and research collaborations, and is maintained by dedicated technical staff.

Innovation and Incubation Centers: IIT Delhi has established technology business incubators, innovation centers, and entrepreneurship cells that provide co‑working spaces, mentoring, seed funding access, intellectual property support, and networking with investors and industry mentors for student and faculty startups; these facilities help transition laboratory research and student projects into viable products and companies, contributing to the broader startup ecosystem and innovation culture on campus.

Lecture Halls and Academic Buildings: The institute’s academic area comprises multiple lecture halls, classrooms, seminar rooms, and auditoria fitted with audio‑visual equipment, projectors, and, increasingly, facilities for hybrid and online teaching; academic buildings are organized around departments and centers, often including faculty offices, meeting rooms, and small discussion spaces that facilitate both formal teaching and informal academic interactions.

Sports and Recreation Facilities: IIT Delhi provides a wide range of sports infrastructure, including playgrounds for cricket, football, and hockey; courts for basketball, tennis, badminton, and volleyball; athletics tracks; a gymnasium and fitness center; and indoor sports areas for table tennis and other activities; these facilities support inter‑IIT and intra‑campus sports events and help students maintain physical fitness and work‑life balance amid demanding academic schedules.

Cultural and Student Activity Centers: Dedicated spaces such as student activity centers, auditoria, amphitheaters, and music and drama rooms support extracurricular activities including music, dance, theater, debating, photography, and literature; student clubs and societies use these facilities to organize workshops, competitions, and flagship cultural festivals like Rendezvous, which draw participation from across India and enrich campus life beyond the classroom.

Health and Medical Services: The campus typically includes a health center or hospital‑type facility that offers primary healthcare, medical consultations, basic diagnostics, and pharmacy services for students, faculty, and staff; arrangements are often in place for emergency care and referrals to larger city hospitals in Delhi, and periodic health camps and awareness programs are conducted to promote well‑being.

Residential Quarters for Faculty and Staff: IIT Delhi’s campus contains residential complexes for faculty members, staff, and their families, contributing to a vibrant on‑campus community where many academic and administrative personnel live near their workplaces; this residential character enhances accessibility, fosters informal academic interaction, and supports participation in campus events and governance beyond office hours.

Campus Transport and Accessibility: Internal roads, pedestrian pathways, and limited campus transport options help students and staff move between hostels, academic buildings, sports facilities, and other areas; the campus is located in Hauz Khas with access to public transportation options such as nearby metro stations and bus routes, facilitating connectivity with the wider Delhi region for internships, industry visits, and leisure activities.

Shops and Essential Services: Within and around the campus, various utility facilities such as small grocery shops, stationery stores, photocopy and print centers, banks or ATMs, and postal or courier services operate to meet everyday needs of students and staff, reducing the need for frequent travel outside campus for basic errands and enabling a self‑contained living and learning environment.

Green Spaces and Campus Environment: The IIT Delhi campus includes landscaped gardens, tree‑lined avenues, and open green spaces that provide pleasant surroundings for walking, outdoor study, and informal gatherings; this relatively green and quiet environment, especially notable given the institute’s urban location in Delhi, supports concentration, relaxation, and a sense of community among residents and visitors.

contact_info.address: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, Hauz Khas, New Delhi – 110016, Delhi, India

university_name: Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (IIT Guwahati)

overview.location: Amingaon, North Guwahati, Assam, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra River, about 20 km from the city centre
overview.campus_size: Approximately 700 acres (~285 hectares) of residential, fully self‑contained campus land on the north bank of the Brahmaputra River[1][7]
overview.description: Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (IIT Guwahati) was established in 1994 as the sixth IIT in India and the first IIT in the North‑Eastern region, with academic programmes beginning in 1995 as part of the country’s push to expand high‑quality technical education across all regions.[4][5] The institute was created under the broader vision of the Government of India to promote advanced engineering, science, and design education, and it has quickly grown from a relatively young campus into a nationally and internationally recognized technological university.[4][1] Located on a scenic, self‑contained campus on the north bank of the Brahmaputra River near Guwahati, Assam, the institute is widely noted for its natural beauty, modern infrastructure, and residential environment that supports an intensive academic and research culture.[1][7] Within a short span, IIT Guwahati has built world‑class infrastructure and state‑of‑the‑art laboratories, enabling cutting‑edge research across engineering, physical sciences, biosciences, healthcare, management, and humanities.[5][8] The institute currently has multiple engineering and science departments, several interdisciplinary centres, and dedicated schools that collectively offer B.Tech., B.Des., BSc(Hons), M.Tech., M.Des., M.Sc., MBA, M.A., and Ph.D. programmes, reflecting a broad academic spectrum that goes well beyond traditional engineering.[5][4] IIT Guwahati has developed a strong reputation in areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, design, environmental science, nanotechnology, biotechnology, and healthcare technologies, and has also been recognized for unique achievements like technology transfer in domains such as animal health vaccines.[1][8] Over the years, the institute has consistently featured among the top engineering institutions in national rankings, and it has steadily advanced in global rankings, reinforcing its status as a premier Indian institution of higher education and research.[1][7] The campus culture is known for being vibrant and student‑centric, with a strong emphasis on technical clubs, cultural and sports festivals, innovation and entrepreneurship cells, and collaboration with industry and international partners, all of which foster holistic development beyond academics.[1][5] Being the only older‑generation IIT in the North‑East, IIT Guwahati plays a crucial role in meeting the aspirations of the region by attracting talent, creating local high‑skill manpower, supporting regional innovation, and acting as a hub for outreach to schools, colleges, and industry in the North‑Eastern states.[5][6] Through its combination of rigorous academics, high‑impact research, strong placement outcomes, and a distinctive setting that blends natural landscape with modern facilities, IIT Guwahati has established itself as a key pillar in India’s science and technology ecosystem and an important contributor to the country’s innovation and knowledge economy.[5][8]

rankings: NIRF 2024 Overall: Ranked 9th in India, reflecting IIT Guwahati’s strong performance across teaching, learning resources, research and professional practice, graduation outcomes, and perception metrics among peers and employers.[1]

NIRF 2024 Engineering: Ranked 7th in the Engineering category, placing IIT Guwahati among the top tier of Indian engineering institutes on parameters such as research output, academic excellence, and industry linkages.[1]

NIRF – Consistent Top 10 Presence: Over recent years, IIT Guwahati has consistently appeared in the top 10 in major NIRF categories, underlining sustained performance rather than a one‑off ranking, and signalling stable quality in academics, research, and placements.[1][5]

QS World University Rankings 2026: Ranked around =334 globally, demonstrating that IIT Guwahati has acquired significant international visibility and competitiveness among world universities, particularly in engineering and technology disciplines.[7]

QS Asia Rankings: IIT Guwahati regularly appears within the better‑ranked segment of Asian universities, indicating strong regional standing in research impact, academic reputation, and international collaborations in the Asian higher education landscape.[7][8]

Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings: IIT Guwahati is listed in THE rankings, with its profile highlighting 11 departments and multiple research centres, which illustrates its research breadth and growing international recognition as a research‑intensive institution.[8]

Subject‑level recognition in Engineering and Technology: In global rankings such as QS and THE, IIT Guwahati frequently attains higher positions in engineering and technology related subject bands compared to its overall university rank, showing particular strength in core technical disciplines.[7][8]

Research and Innovation Recognition: Ranking frameworks and external profiles commonly emphasize IIT Guwahati’s advanced research infrastructure and strong research output, which contribute significantly to indicators like citations per faculty, industry income, and patents.[5][8]

Design and Interdisciplinary Reputation: Being one of the first IITs to introduce full‑fledged design programmes (B.Des and M.Des) and to launch programs such as B.Tech in Data Science & AI has contributed to its reputation in rankings and surveys that value innovation and program diversity.[1]

National and Regional Impact: Beyond formal ranking numbers, IIT Guwahati is widely acknowledged by government agencies and academic bodies as a leading institution of national importance and a central technological hub for the North‑Eastern region, which is reflected in its standing in official profiles and governmental listings.[5][6]

B.Tech.course_name: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
B.Tech.duration: 4 Years (8 Semesters, full‑time residential undergraduate program)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: For general category students, the tuition fee component for the B.Tech program is typically in the range of approximately INR 1.0–1.2 lakh per semester (subject to change as per Government of India and IIT Council regulations), with additional charges for hostel, mess, examination, and one‑time fees like admission and security deposits; fee waivers and concessions are available for SC/ST/PH students and economically weaker sections as per prevailing government norms.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is primarily through the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Advanced after qualifying JEE Main, conducted at the national level; candidates must have completed 10+2 (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, and must meet minimum percentage or percentile requirements specified by JoSAA and IIT Guwahati for the year; 2024 JEE Advanced closing ranks for CSE at IIT Guwahati are around All India Rank ~623 for the open category, indicating very high competition; seat allocation is done through the Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) based on rank, category, and choice filling, and candidates must also satisfy age, attempt, and subject‑combination criteria as mandated for JEE Advanced.[1]

B.Tech.course_name: B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee structure for B.Tech ECE is broadly similar to other B.Tech programs at IIT Guwahati, with per‑semester tuition roughly in the INR 1.0–1.2 lakh range for general category students, plus semester‑wise hostel and mess charges, institute fees, and one‑time charges; eligible students from reserved categories or low‑income backgrounds may receive fee waivers or reduced tuition as per government and institute policies.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is via JEE Advanced, following qualification in JEE Main, and candidates must satisfy all JEE Advanced eligibility criteria including age limits, number of attempts, and minimum marks in 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics; cutoffs vary by year and category, with the 2024 JEE Advanced cut‑off rank for ECE at IIT Guwahati around 1658 in the open category, and seat allocation occurs through centralized JoSAA counselling based on All India Rank and preference order.[1]

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The aggregate tuition fee over four years for Electrical Engineering is comparable to other B.Tech disciplines at IIT Guwahati, typically amounting to several lakhs of rupees for general category students when summed across eight semesters, excluding mess and hostel charges; the institute follows centrally decided tuition norms and offers full or partial fee remissions for certain categories of students as per national guidelines.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Candidates must qualify JEE Main and then JEE Advanced, with eligibility rules regarding 10+2 subjects (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics), year of passing, age, and number of attempts; JoSAA counselling allocates seats to IIT Guwahati’s EE program based on All India Rank in JEE Advanced, category, and choice order, with 2024 cut‑off ranks for EE around 2217 for open category, indicating high competition for limited seats.[1]

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee framework for B.Tech Mechanical Engineering mirrors that of other B.Tech programs at IIT Guwahati, with per‑semester tuition generally in the same band as CSE and ECE for general category students, along with compulsory institute, hostel, and mess fees, and refundable security deposits; financial assistance schemes, including fee waivers and scholarships, are available for eligible students.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is through JEE Advanced on completion of JEE Main, requiring a strong performance in a highly competitive national exam, plus 10+2 (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics and satisfaction of all JEE Advanced eligibility norms; JoSAA counselling determines seat allotment, and in 2024, mechanical engineering at IIT Guwahati had a closing rank around 4523 in the open category, though exact cutoffs vary annually by category and gender.[1]

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: Civil Engineering students pay the same basic B.Tech tuition structure as other branches at IIT Guwahati, with total tuition over four years generally reaching several lakhs of rupees for general category students, plus hostel, mess, and miscellaneous academic charges; fee waivers for SC/ST and other eligible categories are commonly available under institutional and governmental schemes.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Entry is via JEE Advanced after qualifying JEE Main, and candidates must have studied Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics in 10+2 and meet minimum performance and eligibility norms; admission is routed through JoSAA with All India Rank in JEE Advanced as the primary selection metric, and the 2024 closing rank for civil engineering at IIT Guwahati is around 7670 in the open category, reflecting competitive but slightly more accessible entry compared to CSE and ECE.[1]

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: Chemical Engineering follows the standard IIT Guwahati B.Tech fee regime, with tuition assessed each semester at rates broadly aligned with other IITs and subject to periodic revision by government and institute authorities; overall costs include tuition, hostel and mess charges, and various academic and student welfare fees, with a set of scholarships and fee concessions available for deserving students.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Prospective students must clear JEE Main and JEE Advanced, hold a 10+2 qualification with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, and satisfy additional JEE Advanced criteria like age and attempt limits; JoSAA manages centralized counselling and seat allocation, and 2024 cut‑off data indicate that chemical engineering at IIT Guwahati closes at around rank 5363 (open category), though the exact rank fluctuates each year with demand and number of seats.[1]

B.Tech.course_name: B.Tech in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: As a recently introduced, high‑demand program, the B.Tech in Data Science and AI is governed by the same broad fee policy as other B.Tech offerings at IIT Guwahati, with tuition around the standard IIT B.Tech level per semester, plus residential and institute charges; due to its specialized nature, students may also engage with advanced labs and computational infrastructure funded through sponsored research and centre grants without an explicit additional tuition premium.[1][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is via JEE Advanced with eligibility identical in structure to other B.Tech programs (JEE Main qualification, 10+2 with PCM, age and attempt constraints, minimum performance requirements), but the cut‑off rank for Data Science & AI is typically very tight due to high demand nationwide; IIT Guwahati introduced this program in response to industry and research trends, and seat allotment occurs through JoSAA based on JEE Advanced rank and candidate preferences, making it one of the most competitive branches at the institute.[1]

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech (Various Specializations in Engineering and Technology)
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: M.Tech programs at IIT Guwahati generally have lower per‑semester tuition than undergraduate B.Tech for many categories, and total tuition over two years is typically in the range of a few lakhs of rupees for general category students, excluding hostel and mess; many M.Tech students receive stipends via GATE‑based assistantships funded by the Ministry of Education, which can effectively offset a substantial portion of living and academic expenses.[4][5]
M.Tech.eligibility: Admission to M.Tech is primarily through the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) in a relevant discipline, coupled with a qualifying undergraduate degree (B.E./B.Tech or equivalent) with a minimum CPI/percentage set by the department; shortlisting may involve GATE score cutoffs, and some specializations may conduct interviews or written tests, with final selection based on GATE performance, academic record, and departmental criteria, and limited seats also offered to sponsored candidates from industry or government organizations.[5][8]

MBA.total_tuition_fee: The MBA program at IIT Guwahati is a professional postgraduate course with a total tuition fee typically higher than conventional M.Sc programs but broadly aligned with management programs at leading public institutions in India; the fee is charged semester‑wise and covers academic delivery, library and IT usage, and other institute facilities, while hostel, mess, and miscellaneous charges are paid separately, and scholarships or educational loans are commonly used by students to support their study.[5]
MBA.eligibility: Candidates must hold a bachelor’s degree in any discipline with at least the minimum percentage or CGPA prescribed by the institute and are generally required to submit a valid score in a recognized management entrance exam such as CAT (or as specified in that year’s admission brochure); shortlisting is based on entrance test percentile, academic background, and sometimes work experience, followed by group discussions and personal interviews or online selection processes, with final offers extended according to composite scores and category‑wise seat availability.[5]

Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: The B.Des program follows an IIT‑level undergraduate fee structure with semester‑wise tuition plus design‑specific studio and laboratory usage supported by institute infrastructure; total tuition across four years is comparable to B.Tech fees for general category students, and students also pay hostel, mess, and other academic charges, with reserved category fee waivers and centrally sponsored scholarships available based on eligibility.[1][5]
Other Programs.eligibility: IIT Guwahati was the first IIT to launch full‑fledged design programs, and admission to B.Des is via the common design entrance pathway (historically including UCEED and central counselling mechanisms) rather than JEE Advanced; applicants must have completed 10+2 in any stream meeting specified criteria, qualify the relevant design entrance exam, and participate in centralized seat allocation processes, with final admission based on rank, category, and institute choice, under the regulations prevalent for the year of admission.[1]

Other Programs.course_name: M.Sc (Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and allied disciplines)
Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: The total tuition fee for M.Sc programs is generally modest compared to professional programs, with per‑semester academic fees calibrated to encourage high‑quality science education and research, and overall costs including hostel and mess charges; a number of students receive financial support through institute scholarships, national fellowships, or project assistantships depending on performance and funding availability.[4][5]
Other Programs.eligibility: Admission to M.Sc programs is typically via national‑level entrance examinations in the sciences (such as JAM or similar tests notified by IIT Guwahati for specific years), and applicants must hold a relevant bachelor’s degree with specified minimum marks and subject prerequisites; departments may use all‑India ranks and category‑wise cutoffs to offer seats, and some may additionally consider interviews or academic records for final admission decisions.[5][8]

Other Programs.course_name: Ph.D. (Engineering, Sciences, Humanities, Social Sciences, Design, Management)
Other Programs.duration: Typically 3–5 Years (full‑time research program, with possible extension as per regulations)
Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: Ph.D. candidates pay relatively modest semester‑wise tuition and registration fees compared to taught programs, as doctoral education is primarily research‑oriented and often supported by fellowships; many full‑time Ph.D. scholars receive monthly stipends under schemes such as Institute Assistantship, CSIR/UGC/DBT fellowships, or project‑funded positions, which help cover living costs and tuition, and fee remission may be available for certain categories or sponsored candidates from academic and R&D organizations.[5][8]
Other Programs.eligibility: Eligibility norms vary by department but typically require a relevant Master’s degree (or exceptional B.Tech/B.E. with high CPI for direct Ph.D.) in engineering, science, design, management, or humanities, along with qualification in national‑level exams such as GATE, NET, CSIR‑UGC, or equivalent; departments shortlist candidates based on academic record, exam scores, and research interests, and selection usually involves a written test and/or interview to assess research aptitude and fit with departmental research groups, with both full‑time regular, project‑linked, and sponsored Ph.D. categories available.[5][8]

placements.description: IIT Guwahati has built a strong and steadily improving placement record, with its graduates being recruited by leading Indian and multinational companies across technology, consulting, finance, core engineering, research, and analytics domains, reflecting the institute’s academic strength and industry relevance.[2][5] The institute’s Career Development and Placement Cell coordinates campus recruitment drives, pre‑placement talks, aptitude tests, technical interviews, and HR rounds, ensuring that students receive structured support in preparing for placements and interacting with recruiters.[2] Over the years, average and median salary packages for B.Tech and dual degree students have shown an upward trend, driven by increased participation from high‑paying recruiters in sectors such as software product development, quantitative finance, AI/ML, and consulting, as well as by the strong technical portfolio of IIT Guwahati students.[1][5] Core engineering branches also see placements with reputed public and private sector companies in manufacturing, energy, infrastructure, and engineering services, and many students opt for higher studies in leading institutions in India and abroad, which is also considered a positive graduation outcome by ranking frameworks.[5][8] The institute has seen several high domestic packages from technology and product‑based firms, often above the typical averages, and in some years international offers have significantly raised the top CTC figures, demonstrating global employer confidence in the talent pool.[1][7] Internships form an integral part of the career pipeline: many pre‑final year students secure summer internships with major companies through campus processes, and a significant proportion of these internships convert into pre‑placement offers (PPOs), thereby strengthening final placement statistics and giving students early exposure to real‑world projects.[2][5] For postgraduate programs like M.Tech, M.Des, M.Sc, and MBA, placements are aligned with specialization areas—M.Tech students often join R&D, engineering design, or technical consulting roles, MBA graduates enter management roles in operations, marketing, analytics, and finance, and design graduates join UX/UI, product design, and creative technology companies.[5][8] The institute actively engages its alumni network and industry collaborators to enhance placement opportunities, host workshops, coding contests, and hackathons, and bring in more recruiters from emerging sectors such as deep tech startups, fintech, and health tech.[1][5] Placement statistics and recruiter feedback consistently highlight the strong analytical skills, problem‑solving ability, and adaptability of IIT Guwahati graduates, and this reputation reinforces the institute’s standing as a preferred hiring destination in the North‑East and across India.[2][5] While exact package numbers vary year to year due to market conditions and recruiter mix, the overall trend reflects robust campus placement performance, with competitive average CTCs, prominent recruiters, and a broad spectrum of roles, making IIT Guwahati an attractive choice for students seeking both high‑quality education and strong career outcomes.[1][7]
placements.highest_package: Recent high packages (including a mix of domestic and occasional international offers) have reached well into the top decile of CTCs among Indian engineering campuses, with select students in computer science and allied branches receiving very high compensation from product‑based technology companies and global firms; exact figures vary annually and are typically reported in official placement reports and press releases.[1][7]
placements.average_package: Average packages for B.Tech and dual degree programs at IIT Guwahati have been consistently competitive with other leading IITs, commonly falling into the higher single‑digit to low double‑digit lakh per annum band for many branches, with CSE, ECE, and data‑oriented programs generally above the overall average and core branches maintaining solid mid‑range averages; precise numbers differ by batch and are detailed in annual placement statistics published by the institute.[1][5]
major_recruiters: McKinsey & Company (and other top consulting firms in select years)
Public sector and government‑linked organizations visiting in different recruitment cycles

facilities: Central Library: IIT Guwahati’s central library is a major academic resource centre with a large and growing collection of books, reference volumes, journals, theses, and digital resources in engineering, science, design, management, and humanities, and it provides access to numerous online databases, e‑journals, and e‑books, along with dedicated reading rooms, computer terminals, and extended study hours to support intensive coursework and research.[5][7]

Hostels and Residential Facilities: The institute is a fully residential campus with multiple hostels for male and female students, offering well‑furnished rooms, common rooms, recreation areas, Wi‑Fi connectivity, and mess facilities; faculty and staff housing is also provided on campus, creating a closely knit academic community where students and teachers live in proximity and interact beyond classroom hours.[5][7]

Advanced Research Laboratories: IIT Guwahati has developed world‑class, state‑of‑the‑art laboratories across its departments and centres, supporting research in areas such as nanotechnology, biotechnology, advanced materials, artificial intelligence, electronics, environmental engineering, and healthcare; these labs house sophisticated scientific instruments and experimental setups, enabling both fundamental and applied research projects sponsored by national and international agencies.[5][8]

Interdisciplinary Centres and Schools: Several interdisciplinary centres and schools focus on cutting‑edge themes like data science, energy, environment, healthcare, and design, promoting collaborative research across engineering, sciences, management, and humanities, and providing specialized facilities such as high‑performance computing clusters, prototyping workshops, and experimentation platforms for multi‑disciplinary projects.[5][8]

Lecture Halls and Auditoriums: The campus includes a modern lecture hall complex with multiple large lecture theatres, each capable of seating around 250 students, and an auditorium with an approximate capacity of 1500, equipped with audio‑visual systems; these venues are used for regular teaching, workshops, national and international conferences, cultural events, and institute‑wide ceremonies.[7]

Computer and IT Infrastructure: IIT Guwahati maintains strong IT infrastructure with campus‑wide networking, high‑speed internet connectivity, computer centres, departmental computing labs, and specialized clusters for research; students and faculty have access to software tools and platforms needed for programming, data analysis, simulation, and design, supporting both academic and extracurricular technical activities.[5][7]

Sports and Recreation Facilities: The institute provides extensive sports infrastructure including outdoor fields for cricket, football, and athletics, courts for basketball, volleyball, tennis, and badminton, as well as indoor sports facilities and gymnasiums; regular sports events, inter‑hostel tournaments, and fitness programs encourage physical well‑being and a healthy work‑life balance among students.[5][7]

Cultural and Student Activity Spaces: Multiple open‑air and indoor venues exist for cultural clubs, music, dance, drama, literary societies, and student‑run bodies; large‑scale student festivals and technical events make use of these facilities, and dedicated rooms for clubs foster a vibrant campus life that supports creativity, leadership, and teamwork beyond academics.[1][5]

Design and Innovation Studios: As one of the first IITs with full‑fledged design programs, IIT Guwahati hosts specialized studios, design labs, maker spaces, and prototyping workshops in its Department of Design and related centres, equipped with tools for model making, digital fabrication, visualization, and user‑experience research, thereby supporting design education and product innovation.[1][5]

Healthcare and Medical Centre: A campus health centre staffed with medical practitioners and support personnel provides primary healthcare services to students, staff, and faculty, including outpatient care, basic diagnostics, and emergency response support; the institute also maintains arrangements with external hospitals in the city for advanced medical treatment when required.[5]

Cafeterias, Messes, and Shopping Amenities: Each hostel has its own mess facility offering regular meals, and there are additional canteens and cafeterias across campus that serve a variety of cuisines and snacks; essential shopping outlets and small convenience stores within campus provide daily necessities, reducing the need for frequent travel to the city for routine requirements.[5][7]

Transportation and Connectivity: The campus is located around 20 km from the heart of Guwahati city and is connected via road, with institute‑managed transportation and local public transport options facilitating movement between campus and city; internal campus roads, pedestrian paths, and cycling‑friendly routes enable easy access to academic buildings, hostels, and facilities.[7]

Library and Digital Learning Support: In addition to physical collections, the library and IT services enable remote access to subscribed e‑resources, online learning platforms, digital repositories, and lecture recording systems, which support self‑paced learning, blended pedagogy, and extended research work from hostel rooms and faculty offices.[5][7]

Industry Interaction and Incubation Facilities: Through its centres and dedicated office for sponsored research and industrial consultancy, IIT Guwahati offers infrastructure and administrative support for industry‑sponsored projects, consultancy assignments, and startup incubation, including office space, meeting rooms, and in some cases specialized labs for early‑stage product development.[5][8]

Campus Environment and Green Spaces: The IIT Guwahati campus is known for its picturesque natural surroundings, with green areas, water bodies, and an environmentally conscious layout that integrates academic and residential buildings into the landscape; this environment provides a calm and aesthetically pleasing setting conducive to study, reflection, and creative work.[1][7]
