university_name: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IIT Hyderabad)

overview.location: Kandi (near Sangareddy), Telangana, India – on NH-65, close to the Hyderabad Outer Ring Road
overview.type: Public/Government – Institute of National Importance under the Institutes of Technology Act
overview.campus_size: Approximately 576–600 acres of residential, fully planned campus at Kandi, Sangareddy
overview.description: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IIT Hyderabad or IITH) is a premier public technical and research university established in 2008 by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, as part of the expansion of the IIT system to strengthen high‑quality engineering education and research in the country.[2][5] It initially operated from a temporary campus in Hyderabad before shifting in 2015 to its modern, eco‑conscious permanent campus at Kandi, spanning nearly 600 acres with academic blocks, hostels, research facilities, and recreational spaces integrated into a master‑planned layout.[2][7] The institute was developed with significant technical and financial collaboration from the Government of Japan, which helped shape its infrastructure, research ethos, and early academic collaborations.[2] Despite being a relatively young IIT, IIT Hyderabad has rapidly built a strong reputation and is consistently ranked among the top engineering institutes in India in the NIRF rankings, often featuring in the top 10 for engineering and among the leading research institutions nationally.[4][5][6] Internationally, IITH has established a visible presence through its improving QS World University Rankings and Times Higher Education rankings, where it is recognized as one of India’s notable engineering-focused universities with growing global research output.[4][7] The institute emphasizes a "learning by doing" and innovation-driven academic model, reflected in its project-based curriculum, BUILD and BHARATI initiatives, and a strong culture of undergraduate and postgraduate research.[5] Campus life at IIT Hyderabad is characterized by a residential setup where students, faculty, and staff live in close proximity, supported by modern hostels, sports facilities, clubs, and cultural festivals that encourage holistic development beyond academics.[5][7] The institute has invested heavily in advanced laboratories, interdisciplinary centers, and incubation spaces, which have led to thousands of Scopus-indexed publications and hundreds of patents and startups over a short span of time.[4][6] With programs ranging from traditional B.Tech disciplines to niche areas like Artificial Intelligence, Biomedical Engineering, Techno‑Entrepreneurship, and Design, IITH functions as a hub for cutting‑edge education tailored to emerging industry and societal needs.[4][5] Owing to its rapid growth, strong placement records, vibrant research ecosystem, and entrepreneurial culture, IIT Hyderabad is widely regarded as one of the fastest‑rising second‑generation IITs and an important pillar in India’s broader strategy to build world‑class STEM institutions.[4][5][6]

rankings: NIRF 2025 Engineering: Ranked 7th among engineering institutes in India, reflecting strong performance in teaching, learning resources, research output, graduation outcomes, and perception metrics.[6]
NIRF 2025 Innovation: Ranked 6th in the Innovation category, highlighting the institute’s focus on patents, startups, technology transfer, and industry-linked research.[6]

NIRF (recent years) Overall: Consistently placed around 14th–15th in the overall institutional rankings in India, indicating that IITH is competitive even when evaluated alongside multidisciplinary universities and research institutes.[4][6]

NIRF (recent years) Engineering Top‑10: IITH has been "consistently ranked in the top 10 institutes in India for Engineering" according to official institute information, showing sustained excellence rather than a one‑off performance.[5]

QS World University Rankings 2026: Placed around the band of #=664 globally, showing that IIT Hyderabad has secured an identifiable presence in global rankings within less than two decades of its establishment.[4]

QS World Rankings – India Technical Institutes: Counted within the "Top‑7 ranks among technical institutes from India" in QS world rankings, which situates IITH among the leading Indian tech institutions on international parameters.[4]

QS World Rankings – Top 600 Club (earlier editions): Earlier QS cycles placed IIT Hyderabad within or near the "Top 600" globally, and the institute highlights its entry into and retention near this global bracket as a milestone for a young IIT.[4]

National research profile: Cited among the "Top‑12 Research Institutes in the country" in certain NIRF/research‑oriented classifications, underlining the quality and volume of sponsored research, publications, and PhD training.[4][6]

Research output: Approximately 7,500+ Scopus‑indexed publications over about 14 years, which, though not a formal ranking, is used by several ranking frameworks as an indicator of the institute’s research strength and impact.[4]

Innovation & entrepreneurship metrics: Over 630+ patents filed and 335+ startups supported, helping IIT Hyderabad feature strongly in innovation-oriented rankings and government innovation indices that track commercialization and startup ecosystems.[6]

B.Tech.course_name: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: For general/OBCEWS students, the tuition fee is typically in the range of ₹1–2 lakh per semester, with total tuition over four years often around ₹8–10 lakh, excluding hostel, mess, and other charges; substantial tuition waivers or zero tuition are available for SC/ST and many economically weaker-category students as per Government of India and IIT norms, and the institute also offers scholarships, fee remissions, and education loan facilitation for eligible students.[5][6]
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is through JEE (Main) followed by JEE (Advanced), with candidates required to qualify JEE (Advanced) in the relevant year and secure a competitive All India Rank that meets the JoSAA counseling cut-offs for the CSE program at IIT Hyderabad; applicants must have completed Class 12 or equivalent with Physics, Mathematics, and a recognized language/other subjects, satisfying minimum percentage or percentile criteria as prescribed for JEE (Advanced) eligibility, and seat allotment is strictly merit-based with category-wise opening and closing ranks that are typically among the highest at IITH due to the popularity and placement outcomes of CSE.

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee structure is similar to other B.Tech programs, usually around ₹1–2 lakh per semester for general category students, amounting to an estimated ₹8–10 lakh for the full course duration, with additional expenses for hostel, mess, and personal costs; statutory tuition waivers for SC/ST students and income-based fee waivers or remissions for economically weaker students are available, along with institutional and external scholarships for meritorious and needy candidates.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is based on performance in JEE (Advanced) after qualifying JEE (Main), with candidates needing to rank within the relatively tight cut-off range for the AI branch at IIT Hyderabad, which is one of the sought‑after new‑age programs; aspirants must have completed higher secondary education (10+2) with Mathematics and Physics as core subjects and must satisfy JEE (Advanced) eligibility criteria, and final branch allocation is done through centralized JoSAA counseling on the basis of category-wise All India Rank and seat availability.

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee is aligned with other B.Tech programs at IIT Hyderabad, approximating ₹1–2 lakh per semester for general/OBCEWS students, leading to an overall tuition estimate of ₹8–10 lakh over four years, while SC/ST students are generally exempt from tuition as per government norms; hostel, mess, and one‑time charges are additional, and students can avail need‑based financial assistance, national scholarships, and institute-level grants subject to eligibility and availability.[4][5]
B.Tech.eligibility: Selection is through JEE (Advanced) via JoSAA counseling, where candidates who have cleared JEE (Main) and JEE (Advanced) with the required merit can opt for the Biomedical Engineering branch at IIT Hyderabad; applicants must have studied Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics at the 10+2 level and satisfy the age, attempt, and percentage criteria prescribed by the JEE organizing authorities, and the closing ranks for this branch fall within competitive ranges reflecting its niche and interdisciplinary appeal.

B.Tech.course_name: B.Tech in Electrical Engineering / Electronics-related disciplines
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The indicative tuition fee is around ₹1–2 lakh per semester for general category students, with a cumulative tuition outlay of roughly ₹8–10 lakh over the full course, supplemented by hostel, mess, and other institutional fees; SC/ST students benefit from tuition exemptions as per central government policy, and there are scholarships, fee waivers, and assistantships (in later years via research/industry projects) that can reduce the net cost for deserving students.[5][6]
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission occurs via JEE (Advanced) based on All India Rank, with counseling and seat allocation handled through JoSAA; candidates must complete 10+2 with Physics, Mathematics, and typically Chemistry or an equivalent science subject, meet JEE eligibility criteria, and secure a rank within the opening and closing ranges announced for the Electrical/ECE-related B.Tech programs at IIT Hyderabad, which are generally in high demand due to robust placement outcomes and research opportunities.

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering / allied specializations
M.Tech.duration: 2 Years (4 Semesters, full-time; some specializations may offer flexible or sponsored tracks)
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: Tuition fees for M.Tech are typically lower per semester than for B.Tech, and for GATE-qualified students admitted to regular full-time programs, tuition may be around a few tens of thousands of rupees per semester, with total tuition for two years commonly lying in the range of ₹1–2 lakh; many students receive monthly stipends through GATE-based MHRD/Ministry scholarships, and sponsored/part-time candidates may follow different fee structures as per institute and funding agency norms.[5][6]
M.Tech.eligibility: Candidates must possess a relevant B.E./B.Tech (or equivalent) degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or closely related disciplines with a minimum CGPA/percentage prescribed by IIT Hyderabad and must typically have a valid GATE score in CS or another acceptable paper, with shortlisting and admission based on GATE score, academic performance, and sometimes departmental tests or interviews; certain industry-oriented or sponsored M.Tech options may admit experienced professionals using GATE or other criteria, as notified in the institute’s admission brochure.

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech in Artificial Intelligence / Data Science / AI-related fields
M.Tech.duration: 2 Years (4 Semesters, full-time with possible specialization tracks)
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee is generally in a similar band as other M.Tech programs, with per-semester tuition on the order of tens of thousands of rupees for regular GATE-based admissions, and an overall tuition of roughly ₹1–2 lakh across the two-year duration, excluding hostel and living expenses; qualified students often receive GATE-based stipends that partially offset costs, and special executive or online variants of data-centric programs may carry different fee structures reflecting their modular or industry-focused design.[4][5]
M.Tech.eligibility: Applicants must hold a relevant undergraduate degree in engineering or technology, such as CSE, ECE, EE, or allied areas, and usually require a valid GATE score in CS, EC, EE, or other specified papers according to the program brochure, with shortlisting based on GATE performance and further evaluation via interviews or written tests where applicable; some industry-oriented or executive-style offerings in data science or AI may admit candidates with significant work experience under different selection criteria, such as academic record, statement of purpose, and professional track record.

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech in Biomedical Engineering / allied interdisciplinary programs
M.Tech.duration: 2 Years (4 Semesters, full-time, research and project intensive)
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee falls within the usual M.Tech range at IIT Hyderabad, around a few tens of thousands of rupees per semester for regular seats, culminating in approximately ₹1–2 lakh total tuition over the program, with additional hostel and thesis-related expenses; GATE-qualified students are eligible for stipends subject to government rules, and collaborative or sponsored research projects may provide financial support or contingency grants for thesis work.[4][5]
M.Tech.eligibility: Admission generally requires a B.E./B.Tech or equivalent degree in Biomedical Engineering, Electronics, Electrical, Mechanical, Biotechnology, Instrumentation, or related disciplines, along with a valid GATE score in appropriate papers such as BM, EC, EE, IN, ME, or BT, as specified by the department; selection is typically based on GATE score, academic background, and in some cases departmental interviews or technical assessments that evaluate the candidate’s aptitude for interdisciplinary biomedical research.

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech in Techno-Entrepreneurship / industry-oriented M.Tech programs
M.Tech.duration: 2 Years (4 Semesters, with possible flexible or modular structures depending on track)
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: These specialized, often industry-linked M.Tech programs may have fee structures that differ slightly from standard GATE-linked M.Tech offerings, sometimes reflecting additional components like innovation labs, incubation support, or executive-style delivery; in many cases, tuition lies around the low‑to‑mid lakh range for the full program, though exact figures vary by cohort and mode (regular, sponsored, executive), and students may also access seed support or grants through entrepreneurship cells and incubation schemes rather than conventional stipends.[4][5]
M.Tech.eligibility: Eligibility typically includes a relevant engineering or technology bachelor’s degree with a minimum prescribed CGPA/percentage, and for regular tracks, a valid GATE score in an appropriate discipline, while certain techno‑entrepreneurship or industry-oriented variants might consider applicants based on academic merit plus work experience, statement of purpose, and interviews; these programs look for candidates interested in innovation, startups, and product development, and may require presentation of preliminary ideas or portfolios during the selection process.

Other Programs.course_name: M.Sc / M.S (Research) in Sciences and Interdisciplinary Areas
Other Programs.duration: 2 Years for M.Sc (coursework-focused) and typically 2–3 Years for M.S (research-focused), full-time
Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: Tuition for science and research programs is usually moderate compared to professional programs, with per-semester tuition commonly in the lower tens of thousands of rupees and a total estimated tuition of roughly ₹1–1.5 lakh over the full duration for many tracks, excluding hostel and laboratory expenses; eligible students often receive fellowships or stipends from CSIR, UGC, DST, or project grants, particularly in the case of M.S (Research) candidates working on funded projects.[5][6]
Other Programs.eligibility: For M.Sc, candidates generally require a bachelor’s degree in the relevant science discipline (such as Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, or allied fields) and must qualify through national-level exams or institute-specific criteria, sometimes including tests like JAM as per the admission brochure; for M.S (Research), applicants typically need a relevant B.Tech/B.E. or M.Sc degree, a strong academic record, and in many cases a valid GATE or equivalent qualification, with selection based on academic performance and interviews that assess research potential and alignment with faculty interests.

Other Programs.course_name: Ph.D. Programs across Engineering, Sciences, Design, and Liberal Arts
Other Programs.duration: Typically 4–5 Years full-time, with possible variation based on discipline, research progress, and prior qualifications
Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: Ph.D. tuition fees are generally modest, with low per-semester tuition for full-time scholars; the major financial component is usually covered through fellowships or assistantships, as most Ph.D. students receive monthly stipends from government schemes (e.g., Institute fellowships, CSIR/UGC, DST) or sponsored projects, effectively making the net tuition burden limited while providing a sustained stipend for living expenses, contingent on satisfactory academic and research performance.[5][6]
Other Programs.eligibility: Applicants must hold a relevant Master’s degree (or exceptional B.Tech/B.E. with high CGPA in some direct Ph.D. tracks) in engineering, sciences, design, or liberal arts, along with a strong academic record and, for most categories, a valid qualification such as GATE, UGC-NET, CSIR-NET, or equivalent national fellowship; selection is based on shortlisting from the application pool followed by written tests and interviews conducted by departments, where research proposal fit, prior project work, publications, and letters of recommendation play an important role in the final admission decision.

placements.description: The placement scenario at IIT Hyderabad has evolved rapidly, with the institute now achieving outcomes comparable to many of the older IITs across core engineering, software, analytics, and emerging technology sectors.[4][5][6] Over the years, the number of recruiting companies and offers has steadily grown, supported by a dedicated placement office that coordinates pre-placement talks, internship pipelines, and campus recruitment drives with both Indian and international firms.[5][6] Annual campus recruitment typically sees a strong presence from software and IT majors, semiconductor and electronics companies, consulting firms, R&D organizations, and fast-growing startups, ensuring diverse roles for graduates from different departments.[4][6] B.Tech programs in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, and other computing-related disciplines tend to attract some of the highest-paying offers, while core branches like Electrical, Mechanical, Civil, Chemical, and Biomedical also record solid placement rates with reputed companies in their domains.[4][5] The overall compensation trends indicate a healthy mix of high-end packages from global and top-tier Indian technology firms alongside stable, mid-range offers from established engineering, manufacturing, and consulting recruiters, helping maintain a good median salary for the graduating batch.[4][6] Internships play a central role in the placement ecosystem, with many students completing summer internships at leading companies or research labs, often converting these into pre-placement offers (PPOs) that secure job positions well before the final placement season.[5][6] The institute’s emphasis on research and hands-on learning has also translated into strong opportunities in R&D and product-development roles, including positions in chip design, embedded systems, AI/ML engineering, data science, and advanced materials.[4][6] Entrepreneurship and startup pathways are actively encouraged, with some students opting to work on their own ventures incubated within IITH’s startup ecosystem instead of or alongside conventional placement offers, a trend that contributes indirectly to the institute’s placement and innovation profile.[4][6] Over time, average and median CTC figures at IIT Hyderabad have generally shown an upward trajectory, driven by the rising demand for graduates skilled in AI, data science, VLSI, and other high-growth areas, as well as the institute’s growing brand recognition among recruiters.[4][6] Beyond immediate job placements, the training and career guidance ecosystem — including soft-skills training, mock interviews, mentoring by alumni, and domain-specific workshops — helps students prepare for varied career paths such as higher studies in top global universities, research careers, and leadership roles in industry.[5][6]
placements.highest_package: Recent placement cycles have seen some of the top offers from leading technology and product companies reach very high CTC levels (often in the top decile among IITs), with select international or niche roles significantly exceeding the typical domestic package range, though exact figures vary year to year and by domain.[4][6]
placements.average_package: The average cost-to-company (CTC) for B.Tech graduates generally lies in a strong mid-to-upper range compared with peer institutes, with computing and electronics branches registering higher averages and core branches maintaining competitive figures that have risen steadily as more recruiters and diversified roles have been added.[4][6]
major_recruiters: Google (and other major global tech companies for software and systems roles)[4][6]
Microsoft (for software engineering, cloud, and research-oriented roles in India and sometimes abroad)[4][6]
Amazon (including roles in software development, operations, and data-related functions)[4][6]
Flipkart and other large Indian e-commerce platforms offering product and engineering positions[4][6]
Oracle and similar enterprise software firms recruiting for development and database-related roles[4][6]
Infosys and other large Indian IT services companies (e.g., TCS, Wipro, HCL) hiring across branches[4][6]
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) for diversified IT and consulting assignments across domains[4][6]
Wipro Technologies for IT services, digital, and consulting roles across engineering streams[4][6]
HCL Technologies for software, infrastructure, and engineering service roles[4][6]
Qualcomm and other semiconductor companies for VLSI, embedded systems, and hardware roles[4][6]
Intel and similar hardware/R&D companies for chip design, systems, and software-hardware co-design positions[4][6]
NVIDIA and other graphics/AI hardware firms for roles in GPU computing, AI frameworks, and systems[4][6]
Samsung (including Samsung R&D) for electronics, software, and research roles in India and abroad[4][6]
Texas Instruments and other analog/mixed-signal firms for electronics design and validation[4][6]
L&T (Larsen & Toubro) and other core engineering and infrastructure companies for civil and mechanical roles[4][6]
Caterpillar, John Deere, and similar companies for mechanical and manufacturing-related positions[4][6]
Goldman Sachs and other finance/analytics firms offering quantitative and technology-driven roles[4][6]
Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and similar consulting firms for technology consulting and analytics roles[4][6]
Startups incubated within or connected to IITH’s ecosystem, spanning AI, IoT, healthcare tech, and other verticals[4][6]
Public-sector and research organizations that periodically recruit from IIT Hyderabad for technical and scientific roles[5][6]

facilities: Central Library: IIT Hyderabad maintains a central library that supports engineering, sciences, design, and humanities with a growing collection of physical books, technical reports, theses, and an extensive range of e‑resources including e‑journals, databases, standards, and conference proceedings; the library provides digital access, quiet reading spaces, group-study rooms, and extended hours during exam periods to support intensive academic and research activities.[5][7]

Research Laboratories and Advanced R&D Infrastructure: The campus hosts specialized laboratories in areas such as artificial intelligence, data science, VLSI and microelectronics, materials science, additive manufacturing, biomedical engineering, communications, and robotics, many of which are equipped with modern instrumentation, clean-room environments, high-performance computing clusters, and dedicated project spaces to facilitate cutting-edge research and sponsored projects.[4][5][6]

Hostels and Residential Facilities: IIT Hyderabad is a fully residential campus with multiple hostel blocks for male and female students, offering furnished rooms, internet connectivity, common rooms, recreational areas, and mess facilities; the residential design encourages peer learning and community living, and there are on-campus residences for faculty and staff that help build an integrated academic community.[5][7]

Classrooms, Lecture Halls, and Auditoriums: The academic zone includes well-equipped classrooms, lecture theatres, and seminar halls with modern audio-visual systems, projection, and sometimes lecture capture capabilities, enabling interactive teaching, guest lectures, workshops, and conferences; larger auditoriums and multi-purpose halls host institute events, cultural festivals, convocations, and major academic gatherings.[5][7]

Computing and IT Infrastructure: The institute offers robust IT services including campus-wide high-speed network connectivity, wireless internet access in academic and hostel areas, computer labs for different departments, and servers for course management and research; high-performance computing resources support data-intensive and simulation-based research in areas like AI, materials, CFD, and computational biology.[4][5][6]

Innovation, Incubation, and Startup Support (Research Park, Incubators): IIT Hyderabad has dedicated incubation spaces and a research park with large floor areas (around 1.5 lakh square feet each for incubation and research park activities) to host startups, industry labs, and collaborative projects; these facilities provide office space, mentoring, prototyping support, access to labs, and networking opportunities, underpinning the institute’s strong startup culture.[4][6]

Workshops and Maker Spaces: Departments maintain mechanical, electrical, and interdisciplinary workshops with machine tools, fabrication equipment, electronics benches, 3D printers, and prototyping resources that support the "learning by doing" philosophy; these spaces are crucial for course projects, capstone designs, hackathons, and student competition teams building robots, vehicles, or other engineering prototypes.[5][6]

Sports and Recreational Facilities: The campus includes open and indoor sports facilities such as grounds and courts for cricket, football, basketball, volleyball, and badminton, along with areas for athletics and indoor games; students can participate in inter-IIT tournaments, intramural leagues, and fitness activities that contribute to a balanced campus life.[5][7]

Cultural, Co-curricular, and Student Activity Spaces: Various clubs and student bodies operate from designated rooms and common spaces, organizing activities in music, drama, dance, literature, photography, coding, robotics, and entrepreneurship; the campus hosts cultural and technical fests, talks, and competitions that leverage auditoriums, open-air stages, and student centers for large-scale events.[5][7]

Cafeterias, Messes, and Food Courts: Multiple messes attached to hostels and central dining facilities provide vegetarian and non-vegetarian meals, with menus decided often in consultation with student bodies; additional canteens and cafes across the campus serve snacks and beverages, offering informal spaces for social interaction and group discussions beyond classrooms.[5][7]

Health Centre and Wellness Services: A campus health centre staffed with medical professionals provides primary healthcare services, emergency care, and basic diagnostics for students, faculty, and staff; wellness initiatives may include counselling support, mental health awareness programs, and collaborations with specialized hospitals in Hyderabad for advanced medical treatment when required.[5][7]

Transportation and Internal Mobility: The campus layout, spread over more than 500 acres, is supported by internal roads, walkways, and often shuttle or bus services connecting hostel zones with academic and administrative buildings; its proximity to the Outer Ring Road and NH‑65 facilitates connectivity to Hyderabad city, airports, and major transport hubs for commuting guests, recruiters, and visitors.[2][7]

Administrative and Student Support Services: Dedicated offices manage academic administration, finance, scholarships, international relations, industry relations, career services, and hostel administration, providing structured support for student life-cycle events from admission to graduation; student grievance cells, anti-ragging committees, and mentorship frameworks help maintain a safe and inclusive campus environment.[5][6]

Design and Liberal Arts Spaces: In line with its unique blend of engineering, design, and liberal arts, IIT Hyderabad houses studios, design labs, and creative spaces tailored to design and humanities programs, where students can work on visual communication, product design, and interdisciplinary projects combining technology with social science and artistic perspectives.[4][5]

Green and Sustainable Campus Features: The Kandi campus incorporates environmentally conscious planning with green spaces, efficient water and energy management, and an emphasis on sustainable building practices, aligning with modern campus design principles and providing a pleasant, low‑congestion environment for academic and residential life.[2][7]

university_name: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (IIT Kanpur)

overview.campus_size: Approximately 430 hectares (around 1050+ acres) of fully residential, self-contained campus on the Grand Trunk Road near Kalyanpur, Kanpur district.[1][3]
overview.description: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (IIT Kanpur) is a premier public institute of technology established in 1959, and is recognized as an Institute of National Importance by the Government of India under the Institutes of Technology Act.[1][5] It began operations in late 1959 on the borrowed premises of Harcourt Butler Technological Institute with around 100 students and a small faculty, and later moved in 1963 to its present, meticulously planned campus on the Grand Trunk Road near Kalyanpur in Kanpur district.[1][2] The campus was designed by renowned architect Achyut Kanvinde and is known for its modernist layout, generous green spaces, and a design philosophy aimed at environmental openness, ease of movement, and strong interconnection among academic, residential, and recreational zones.[1] During its formative decade, IIT Kanpur was uniquely shaped by the Kanpur Indo-American Programme (KIAP), under which a consortium of nine leading US universities—including MIT, Caltech, UC Berkeley, Princeton, Carnegie Mellon, University of Michigan, Ohio State, Case Western Reserve, and Purdue—helped set up advanced laboratories, curricula, and research culture.[1][4] Under this Indo-American collaboration, IIT Kanpur became one of the first institutions in India to establish a strong research-driven engineering and science ecosystem, laying the foundation for its later reputation as a global center of excellence in technology and innovation.[1][3] IIT Kanpur is historically significant for introducing one of the earliest formal Computer Science education programs in India, starting computer courses as early as 1963 on an IBM 1620 and launching independent M.Tech and PhD programs in Computer Science and Engineering by 1971, which later evolved into a full-fledged department.[1] Over the decades, the institute has consistently ranked among the top engineering institutions in India and holds a strong position in global rankings, reflecting its high-quality teaching, cutting-edge research, and robust industry linkages.[3] Its alumni and faculty have been recognized with numerous national and international honors, including multiple Padma awards and Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prizes, underlining the institute’s impact on science, technology, policy, and entrepreneurship in India.[1] The campus culture at IIT Kanpur is known for its intense academic rigor balanced with a vibrant student life that includes major technical, cultural, and entrepreneurial festivals such as Techkriti and Antaragni, along with a strong tradition of clubs, student-led initiatives, and competitive sports.[1][3] In recent years, IIT Kanpur has expanded its interdisciplinary footprint through new centers of excellence, incubation programs like the Startup Innovation and Incubation Centre (SIIC), and major national missions in areas such as advanced materials, defense technologies, clean energy, and digital innovation, reinforcing its role as a key driver of India’s scientific and technological advancement.[3]

rankings: NIRF 2024 Engineering: Among the top Indian engineering institutions (historically in top 5), reflecting strong performance in teaching, learning, research, graduation outcomes, and industry perception; exact 2024 rank should be verified from the official NIRF portal as ranks are updated annually based on new data (inference based on its repeated top-tier presence and NIRF methodology).

NIRF 2024 Overall: Consistently placed among the top multi-disciplinary higher education institutions in India, driven by high-quality research output, strong faculty credentials, patents, and a strong ecosystem for innovation and entrepreneurship (approximate position historically within national top 10, to be checked against the latest official NIRF list).

QS World University Rankings 2026: Ranked around **#222 globally** as per QS World University Rankings 2026, positioning IIT Kanpur as one of the leading technical universities worldwide and highlighting its growing international visibility in research and academic reputation.[3]

QS Asia University Rankings: Regularly ranked among the leading universities in Asia in engineering and technology disciplines, reflecting strong academic reputation, employer reputation, faculty–student ratio, and citation impact within the Asian region (exact rank varies year to year and should be taken from the current QS Asia edition).

QS World University Rankings by Subject (Engineering & Technology): Frequently placed among the top Indian institutions and within competitive global bands for core engineering subjects such as Computer Science, Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Mechanical, Civil, and Chemical Engineering, underlining the depth of its technical programs and research strength (based on repeated representation in QS subject tables).

Times Higher Education (THE) World University Rankings – Engineering & Technology: Featured as one of India’s better-performing institutions in engineering and technology categories with strong scores in industry income and research, illustrating IIT Kanpur’s robust industry linkages and applied research impact (exact rank should be referenced from the latest THE subject rankings).

National and governmental recognition: Declared an **Institute of National Importance** under the Institutes of Technology Act, which is an institutional status rather than a numerical rank but effectively places IIT Kanpur in the top policy tier of Indian higher education institutions in engineering and technology.[1][5]

Reputation among employers and research organizations: Consistently reported by national media and industry surveys as a preferred recruitment and collaboration destination for top technology firms, R&D labs, and startups, owing to its rigorous curriculum, strong fundamental training, and active innovation ecosystem (inferred from its strong placement records and QS employer reputation indicator).[3]

Innovation and startup ecosystem recognition: Frequently highlighted for its Startup Innovation and Incubation Centre (SIIC), which hosts several dozen incubated companies and successful graduates, contributing significantly to IIT Kanpur’s perception as a leading innovation-driven campus with one of the stronger incubation ecosystems in the IIT system.[3]

B.Tech.course_name: B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: For Indian nationals, the tuition fee for B.Tech programs at IITs is typically on the order of INR 1–2 lakh per semester, with additional charges for hostel, mess, and other facilities; the exact fee for IIT Kanpur’s B.Tech CSE program is periodically revised by the institute and must be verified from the official IIT Kanpur admissions/fees pages, but students can generally expect a total program cost (tuition only) in the range of roughly INR 8–12 lakh over four years, excluding living and miscellaneous expenses (inference based on prevailing IIT fee norms; exact figures not specified directly in the retrieved sources).
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission is primarily through the national-level Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Advanced, for which candidates must first qualify JEE Main and satisfy age, attempt, and educational criteria prescribed by the Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) and IIT system; only top-ranking JEE Advanced candidates meeting IIT Kanpur’s category-wise opening and closing ranks for CSE (typically among the very highest in India) are allotted seats, and they must also satisfy minimum marks in Class 12 (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics as core subjects; detailed cutoffs and seat matrices are published annually by JoSAA and vary by category, gender, and year (inference using the standard IIT admission framework and IIT Kanpur’s high demand).

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition structure is aligned with the general B.Tech fee regime at IIT Kanpur and other centrally funded IITs, with per-semester tuition on the order of INR 1–2 lakh for general category students, along with hostel, mess, and one-time charges; fee waivers or subsidies may apply for certain economically weaker categories as per Government of India and IIT Kanpur policies; actual payable amounts, including refundable deposits and other components, are published in the institute’s official fee schedules and are subject to periodic revision.
B.Tech.eligibility: Candidates must qualify JEE Advanced after clearing JEE Main and meet the eligibility norms of the IIT system, including passing the 10+2 (or equivalent) examination with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics and meeting the prescribed percentage or rank criteria; seat allocation in Electrical Engineering at IIT Kanpur is done through JoSAA counseling based on JEE Advanced AIR and category-specific opening and closing ranks, which historically are among the top for core engineering branches; reservation policies for SC, ST, OBC-NCL, EWS, and PwD candidates apply as per Government of India rules.

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: Tuition fees follow the standard IIT Kanpur B.Tech structure, with semester-wise tuition typically in the high five-figure to low six-figure INR range for domestic students, plus charges for hostel accommodation, mess advance, medical insurance, and other campus services; scholarship schemes, fee waivers, and educational loans are available for eligible students, but the precise breakup of fees—tuition, institute fees, and refundable components—must be checked from the institute’s current fee notification.
B.Tech.eligibility: Entry is through JEE Advanced based national counseling (JoSAA), and only candidates who successfully clear JEE Main and then perform well in JEE Advanced can register; Mechanical Engineering has competitive cutoffs, though often slightly lower than CSE and EE, and candidates must satisfy minimum performance in 10+2 with PCM subjects; final seat allocation depends on rank, category, seat availability, and preferences locked during counseling, and all admitted students must also conform to medical fitness criteria specified by the IIT system.

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee framework is the same as for other B.Tech programs at IIT Kanpur, with a uniform tuition component and additional institute, hostel, and mess fees; total expenditure over four years can reach into several lakhs of rupees in tuition alone, but need-based financial assistance, scholarships, and government schemes (such as fee remission for lower income groups) can significantly reduce net payable amounts for eligible students; the institute issues detailed semester-wise fee circulars for each academic year.
B.Tech.eligibility: Admission requires qualifying JEE Advanced, after clearing JEE Main and satisfying age and attempt limits; candidates must have completed 10+2 (or equivalent) with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, achieving minimum marks and rank cutoffs specified for Chemical Engineering; JoSAA counseling handles seat allocation, and category-wise closing ranks for IIT Kanpur provide the effective cutoff for each admission cycle; reservation and relaxation norms are followed as mandated by the Government of India.

B.Tech.total_tuition_fee: Civil Engineering students pay the same base B.Tech tuition as other undergraduate engineering programs at IIT Kanpur; the total fee includes tuition, registration and examination charges, hostel seat rent, mess advance, and various student welfare and facility usage charges; while the absolute numbers change with government policy and inflation, the B.Tech tuition structure remains centrally notified and in line with other IITs, with possibilities of partial or full waivers for students from economically weaker backgrounds according to current regulations.
B.Tech.eligibility: Prospective students must clear JEE Advanced after JEE Main and then participate in JoSAA counseling, listing IIT Kanpur and Civil Engineering as preferred choices; admission is merit-based as per All India Rank in JEE Advanced and is subject to meeting minimum 10+2 PCM marks requirements; Civil Engineering usually has somewhat broader cutoff bands than CSE and EE but still attracts strong ranks given IIT Kanpur’s reputation in infrastructure, structural engineering, and geotechnical research, and all standard IIT category and reservation policies apply.

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: M.Tech programs at IIT Kanpur generally have a per-semester tuition in the mid five-figure INR range for Indian students, along with institute, hostel, and mess charges; many M.Tech students receive financial assistance or stipends through GATE-based scholarships sponsored by the Government of India, which offset a significant portion of the living cost; the exact tuition and fee components for CSE M.Tech are published by IIT Kanpur’s postgraduate admissions office and can vary by category and year.
M.Tech.eligibility: Applicants must possess a relevant B.E./B.Tech or equivalent degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or closely related disciplines with a minimum CGPA/percentage specified by IIT Kanpur; a valid GATE score in Computer Science and Information Technology (CS) is typically required for admission and funding consideration, and shortlisting may be based on GATE score cutoffs, prior academic record, and sometimes interviews or written tests as per department norms; sponsored and part-time candidates may have slightly different eligibility conditions, including work experience requirements.

M.Tech.course_name: M.Tech in Electrical Engineering (with specializations such as Power, Communications, Microelectronics)
M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: The tuition structure for M.Tech in Electrical Engineering is similar to other M.Tech programs at IIT Kanpur, comprising a tuition component, semester registration, and hostel and mess charges; GATE-qualified full-time students often receive monthly stipends funded by MHRD/AICTE (subject to prevailing policies), which help cover living expenses; international students or sponsored candidates may have different fee slabs, which are detailed in IIT Kanpur’s official postgraduate fee schedules.
M.Tech.eligibility: Eligibility usually requires a B.E./B.Tech (or equivalent) in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or allied branches with a specified minimum CGPA or percentage; a valid GATE score in an appropriate paper such as EE, EC, or IN is normally essential for regular full-time admission with scholarship; selection is merit-based, often purely on GATE score but may also involve additional departmental screening such as interviews, and candidates must satisfy institute-wide academic and medical fitness norms; sponsored, part-time, or project-funded seats may have alternative criteria.

M.Tech.total_tuition_fee: M.Tech Mechanical students pay postgraduate-level tuition and associated charges that are generally lower per semester than B.Tech tuition but still substantial; GATE-qualified students admitted under regular schemes typically receive monthly stipends and contingency grants, reducing the effective cost; fees for hostel accommodation, mess, and health insurance remain comparable to other postgraduate students at IIT Kanpur, and the total cost over two years depends on the number of semesters registered and any extended duration beyond the normal program length.
M.Tech.eligibility: Candidates must hold a B.E./B.Tech degree in Mechanical Engineering or closely related disciplines with minimum academic performance criteria set by IIT Kanpur; a valid GATE score in Mechanical Engineering (ME) or an appropriate related paper is generally mandatory for full-time admission, and cutoffs vary by year, specialization, and category; some seats may be reserved for sponsored candidates from industry or government organizations, who are typically exempt from GATE but must fulfill experience and employer-sponsorship requirements and may not receive GATE-based stipends.

MBA.course_name: MBA (Master of Business Administration) – Industrial and Management Engineering (IME)
MBA.total_tuition_fee: The MBA program at IIT Kanpur’s Department of Industrial and Management Engineering generally has a professional program fee structure that is higher than typical M.Tech/M.Sc tuition and is closer to market-aligned management education costs, payable semester-wise; this includes tuition, academic and institute charges, and may exclude hostel and mess expenses which are billed separately; scholarships, teaching assistantships, or loans may be available for deserving candidates, and exact fee figures are provided in the official MBA admission brochure each year.
MBA.eligibility: Candidates typically require a bachelor’s degree in any discipline with a minimum percentage or CGPA set by IIT Kanpur and must possess a valid CAT (Common Admission Test) score for domestic applicants; shortlisting is usually based on CAT percentile, academic record, work experience, and possibly other parameters, followed by a selection process that can include personal interviews, group discussions, and written ability tests conducted by the IME department; for international or sponsored candidates, alternative tests like GMAT and different evaluation criteria may be considered, subject to IIT Kanpur’s MBA admission policies.

Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: The tuition fee for M.Sc programs is usually lower than for B.Tech and M.Tech programs but still involves semester-wise tuition, registration, hostel, and mess components; funded positions under national scholarships or institute assistantships may be available for some M.Sc students based on performance and schemes in force; total fees and any applicable waivers must be verified from IIT Kanpur’s latest fee circular for postgraduate and M.Sc students.
Other Programs.eligibility: Admission to the M.Sc Physics program is typically through national-level exams such as JAM (Joint Admission Test for M.Sc) conducted by the IITs; candidates must hold a bachelor’s degree with Physics as a major or core subject and meet minimum marks/CGPA criteria; final selection is based on JAM rank, category-wise cutoffs, and fulfillment of basic eligibility conditions in mathematics and other supporting subjects, as well as verification of documents and academic records during counseling.

Other Programs.course_name: PhD (Doctor of Philosophy) – Engineering and Sciences
Other Programs.duration: Typically 4–5 years (minimum 3 years, subject to progress and thesis completion)
Other Programs.total_tuition_fee: PhD scholars at IIT Kanpur generally pay a modest tuition and semester registration fee compared to coursework programs, with most full-time PhD students receiving institute, project-based, or external fellowships that include monthly stipends and sometimes contingency grants; hostel fees, mess charges, and health insurance remain applicable, but the net out-of-pocket academic cost can be relatively low due to fellowship support; exact fee details vary by department, funding source, and whether the candidate is full-time, part-time, external, or sponsored.
Other Programs.eligibility: Eligibility for PhD admission usually requires a master’s degree (M.Tech/M.E./M.Sc/MBA or equivalent) in a relevant field with strong academic performance, though exceptional B.Tech/BS graduates from IITs with high CGPAs may be admitted directly to PhD; candidates must also have a valid national-level qualification such as GATE, CSIR-UGC NET, or an equivalent test, unless exempted as per IIT Kanpur norms (e.g., certain categories of IIT graduates or sponsored candidates); selection involves departmental shortlisting, written tests and/or interviews, evaluation of research potential, and assessment of alignment with faculty expertise and departmental research priorities.

placements.description: IIT Kanpur has a long-standing reputation for strong campus placements, with its graduates being sought after by leading technology companies, consulting firms, core engineering enterprises, financial institutions, and research organizations, both in India and abroad.[3] The institute’s placement season is highly structured, beginning with internships and pre-placement offers for pre-final year students and culminating in a multi-phase recruitment drive where hundreds of organizations participate through on-campus and virtual modes coordinated by the institute’s Career Development and Placement Cell.[3] Trends over recent years indicate that IIT Kanpur consistently achieves very high placement percentages for B.Tech and dual-degree programs in high-demand branches such as Computer Science, Electrical, and Mathematics & Computing, while core branches like Mechanical, Civil, and Chemical also record robust outcomes with a mix of core and non-core roles.[3] According to recent media reports, the 2025–26 placement season opened with a record-breaking Day 1 performance, where IIT Kanpur received about 672 job offers on the first day alone, representing roughly a 16% increase compared to the previous year and underscoring the growing employer interest in its students.[8] Over the years, domestic average salary packages for top branches have typically been well into double-digit lakhs per annum for B.Tech students, with median values reflecting steady improvement as more high-end technology, product, and finance roles come to campus (exact numerical averages vary year by year and are usually published by the institute in its official placement reports).[3][8] In addition to domestic roles, a sizeable number of international offers—especially for software engineering, quantitative finance, and research positions—are regularly reported, with some students securing very high-valued compensation packages when converted to Indian rupees, though the institute and media often differentiate between cost-of-living-adjusted international CTCs and Indian offers.[3][8] Internship opportunities are also a major strength, with pre-final year students interning at top companies, overseas research labs, and universities, often through dedicated internship drives and institute-facilitated programs, which frequently convert to pre-placement offers and significantly de-risk the final placement process.[3] The presence of a strong research and startup ecosystem through SIIC and various Centers of Excellence means that some students opt for research positions, higher studies, or entrepreneurial ventures rather than traditional corporate roles, diversifying the placement outcomes beyond pure salary statistics.[3] In recent years, IIT Kanpur has also enhanced engagement with public sector units, government organizations, and mission-mode national projects, enabling interested students to take up impactful roles in policy, infrastructure, and national security-related domains. Overall, the placement scenario at IIT Kanpur is characterized by high offer volumes, rising average CTCs over time, broad sectoral representation, and strong recruiter loyalty, reaffirming the institute’s standing as a preferred hiring destination in India’s technology and innovation landscape.[3][8]
placements.highest_package: Recent placement drives have reported some of the highest cost-to-company (CTC) figures as very high-value international offers in technology and quantitative roles, with annual packages (on a CTC basis and converted to INR) reaching into the crore-plus range, though such figures may represent only a small number of offers and include stock options and benefits; exact numerical highest packages for the latest season are typically released by IIT Kanpur’s placement cell or via official press notes and should be consulted for precise amounts.[3][8]
placements.average_package: Average packages for B.Tech and dual-degree programs at IIT Kanpur in recent years have generally fallen into a healthy double-digit lakh per annum band for domestic offers, with branch-wise averages for CSE and related disciplines often significantly exceeding the institute-wide average; M.Tech, M.Sc, and MBA programs also report competitive average CTCs aligned with their respective industry sectors, and year-on-year trends indicate a gradual upward trajectory in both mean and median compensation figures (exact rupee values are documented in institute placement reports and may change each season).[3][8]
major_recruiters: Google DeepMind / other advanced ML/AI divisions (as applicable to specific years)
Samsung (including Samsung Research centers in India and abroad)
Adani Group and associated technology/infra entities
Public Sector Units (various PSUs such as ONGC, IOCL, HPCL, NTPC, BHEL, depending on year-wise participation)

facilities: PK Kelkar Central Library: A large, modern central library named after IIT Kanpur’s first director, housing a vast collection of books, journals, technical reports, theses, e-resources, and digital databases across engineering, science, humanities, and management; it offers spacious reading halls, digital catalog access, online journal subscriptions, and extended hours to support intensive academic and research work.[1]

Extensive Hostel System: A network of multiple boys’ and girls’ hostels providing residential accommodation to a large proportion of the more than 10,000-strong student body, with facilities such as furnished rooms, common rooms, TV rooms, indoor games, Wi-Fi or wired internet, and messes serving structured meal plans, aiming to create a cohesive residential and learning community on campus.[2]

Advanced Research Laboratories: State-of-the-art research labs spread across departments and interdisciplinary centers, including specialized facilities in microelectronics, nanotechnology, materials science, robotics, computer science, data science, and environmental engineering, many of which were originally set up and expanded with technical support from the Kanpur Indo-American Programme and have since evolved into nationally significant research hubs.[1][3][4]

National Wind Tunnel Facility (NWTF): A major national facility hosted at IIT Kanpur that provides advanced wind tunnel testing capabilities for aerospace, automotive, civil, and defense applications, supporting both academic research and industry-sponsored projects and making the institute a key player in aerodynamics and flight-related experimentation at the national level.[3]

Flight Laboratory with Functional Runway: A modern flight laboratory featuring a functional airstrip and aviation equipment that enables hands-on training, experiments, and demonstrations in aerodynamics, flight mechanics, and aerospace engineering, positioning IIT Kanpur uniquely among Indian academic institutions with such on-campus aviation infrastructure.[3]

High-Performance Computing and Supercomputing Resources: IIT Kanpur historically installed one of the earliest supercomputers in an Indian academic institution and continues to operate high-performance computing (HPC) clusters to support computational research in areas such as fluid dynamics, materials modeling, climate science, and data-intensive machine learning, accessible to faculty and students under structured allocation policies.[3]

Startup Innovation and Incubation Centre (SIIC): A dedicated innovation and incubation ecosystem hosting dozens of technology startups and spin-offs, offering office space, labs, mentorship, seed funding access, IP support, and industry connect; more than 60+ startups have graduated from SIIC and several dozen remain actively incubated, contributing to job creation and commercialization of IIT Kanpur’s research.[3]

Lecture Halls and Academic Complexes: Multiple centrally air-conditioned lecture halls, classrooms, and department buildings equipped with modern teaching aids such as digital projectors, audio systems, and smart boards, complemented by smaller tutorial rooms, seminar rooms, and faculty offices that foster interactive pedagogy and close student–faculty engagement.[1][3]

Central Academic and Administrative Facilities: Administrative buildings, academic offices, and service centers that coordinate academic programs, research administration, sponsored projects, student services, and external collaborations, providing the institutional backbone for the institute’s complex multi-departmental operations.[1][4]

Sports and Recreation Infrastructure: A wide range of sports facilities including large playgrounds for cricket, football, hockey, and athletics, indoor courts for badminton and squash, tennis courts, gymnasiums, and likely swimming and fitness centers, supporting both competitive sports teams and recreational activities that are integral to student life (inferred from typical large IIT campus infrastructure and IIT Kanpur’s residential campus nature).

Student Activity Centers and Clubs: Dedicated spaces for cultural, technical, and hobby clubs that host activities related to music, dance, drama, photography, robotics, coding, literary arts, and entrepreneurship, along with venues and infrastructure for large-scale festivals such as Techkriti (technical festival) and Antaragni (cultural festival), which attract national-level participation.[1][3]

Health Centre and Medical Services: An on-campus health center providing primary medical care, emergency services, and referral support to students, faculty, and staff, often supplemented by tie-ups with city hospitals for specialized treatment; the facility supports preventive health programs, vaccinations, and health-awareness initiatives typical of large residential institutes.

On-Campus Shopping and Dining: Various canteens, cafeterias, snack outlets, and small shops distributed across the campus, including near hostels and academic areas, offering everyday essentials, stationery, groceries, and diverse food options, thereby making the campus largely self-contained and convenient for residents.

Residential Quarters for Faculty and Staff: A sizeable inventory of apartments and staff housing integrated into the campus layout, providing convenient living arrangements for faculty and staff and enabling a vibrant, 24x7 academic community where students can interact with mentors beyond formal classroom hours.[2]

Green and Planned Campus Environment: Extensive green cover, tree-lined avenues, landscaped gardens, and pedestrian-friendly pathways that reflect the original campus planning vision of Achyut Kanvinde, promoting a healthy, aesthetically pleasing, and environmentally conscious setting conducive to both contemplation and collaboration.[1]
